pages.x: In 1206 the tribes of the Mongolian steppe gathered by the Onon river and proclaimed a chief named Temüjin their Genghis Khan, universal ruler. He had united them by war and by sharing the spoils, and he organised every man in units of ten, a hundred, a thousand and ten thousand.
Every Mongol warrior had several horses and rode from childhood, shooting a powerful bow at full gallop.
pages.fx: Their armies moved faster than any other in the world. They learned siege machines from Chinese and Persian engineers, and they used terror: cities that gave in might be spared.

pages.x: In 1211 Genghis attacked the Jin empire of northern China, and in 1215 took its capital, Zhongdu, now Beijing, which was said to have burned for a month.

In 1218 a governor of the Khwarazm Shah killed a Mongol trade caravan at Otrar. The revenge was terrible: Bukhara, Samarkand, Merv and Nishapur were taken, and in some nearly everyone was killed. In all, the Mongol wars may have cost tens of millions of lives.
pages.of: dead in the Mongol wars, perhaps

pages.x: Genghis died in 1227. Under his son Ögedei, Mongol armies crushed the Russian princes, burned Kyiv in 1240 and beat the Poles and the Hungarians in 1241. Then news came that Ögedei had died, and the generals turned back to choose a new khan. Europe was spared.

In 1258 Genghis's grandson Hulagu took Baghdad, the city of the caliphs for five centuries. The caliph was killed, rolled in a carpet and trampled by horses, it was said, and the books of its libraries were thrown in the Tigris until it ran black with ink.

pages.t: Ain Jalut and the divine winds
pages.x: In 1260 the Mamluks of Egypt beat a Mongol army at Ain Jalut, in Palestine, one of the first great Mongol defeats. Far to the east, storms wrecked the fleets that Kublai Khan sent against Japan in 1274 and 1281. The Japanese called them kamikaze, divine winds.

Kublai conquered the Song and became emperor of all China, founder of the Yuan dynasty, ruling from a new capital at Beijing. The empire had split into four khanates, but its roads were safe enough for Marco Polo to travel across Asia to Kublai's court.

The Mongols killed millions and destroyed great cities, but their empire also joined East and West. Trade, ideas, paper money and gunpowder moved across it, and so did the Black Death. Genghis Khan is a national hero in Mongolia today.
pts: The largest land empire in history
From Korea to Hungary in two generations
Joined Asia and Europe, for good and ill
